correctness.rationale: For fixed m, exact Kunz coordinates identify Apéry primitives with strict nontrivial pair inequalities. When g>m, no primitive m is effective and any non-primitive maximal Apéry element forces a Kunz equality, so zero-child vectors lie on finitely many proper codimension-one affine hyperplanes. Two effective Apéry elements lie in a length-m interval, forcing a coordinate near-tie x_i-x_j∈{-1,0,1}; these also form proper hyperplanes. Their intersections with the genus simplex have O_m(g^(m-3)) integer points. An open balanced Kunz interior box gives Theta_m(g^(m-2)) total points. A full relative open box on x1=x2, with x1=x2 the largest coordinates, gives Omega_m(g^(m-3)) semigroups with >=2 children for m>=4; the m3 parity construction gives Omega(1). These logically prove the full assertion. A standalone direct-membership checker cross-validates 1275 semigroups, but finite tests are not the proof.

originality.rationale: Casas–Madrid–Rosales motivates internal/leaf classification; García-Sánchez et al handle specific low multiplicities; Alhajjar–Russell–Steward already prove density one of maximal embedding dimension, which does not imply the new sharp degree-one law. The present all-fixed-m theorem gives Theta_m(g^(m-3)) semigroups with 2+ children and an O_m(g^(m-3)) bound on all !=1 cases. No dominating general implication was located in relevant inspected accessible text or searches. Priority remains provisional because the 2019 full text was inaccessible.
residual_risks: Historical originality is qualified: the inaccessible 2019 full text might contain an equivalent or dominating all-multiplicity degree-one argument. No whole-document NOT_COVERING assertion is made for it.
General Kunz-polytope lattice counting is known; the original contribution is the sharp one-child deviation scale, not maximal-embedding-dimension concentration or the base counting lemma.

value.rationale: The number of effective generators is the natural offspring statistic in the classical numerical-semigroup tree and a central object of the 2026 internal-node conjecture. The theorem gives a previously unprovided sharp, nontrivial universal fixed-multiplicity concentration law with a matching two-child lower bound. It explains why almost all fixed-m semigroups are one-child while quantifying rare branching, and gives eventual internal-node predominance without claiming a finite-genus all-m conjecture. A density-one MED statement alone is insufficient, preserving substantive motivation.
